title: ngAP: Non-blocking Large-scale Automata Processing on GPUs
problem: GPU automata processing suffers from underutilized threads due to insufficient parallelism when processing symbols sequentially, significant redundant computations from repeated state-symbol matches, and poor data locality caused by dynamic thread-to-state mapping.
motivation: Automata serve as compute kernels for high-throughput applications, but GPU potential remains underutilized despite increasing compute power.
method: Instead of processing one input symbol at a time and waiting for it to complete, the system processes multiple symbols in parallel. It prefetches results and stores previously calculated results in lookup tables to avoid redundant computations. By keeping each thread's work isolated, the thread consistently accesses the same data, keeping it in fast local cache rather than requiring slower memory accesses.
key_novelty: The core idea is processing multiple input symbols in parallel instead of one at a time, which enables optimizations like prefetching results and reusing previous calculations.
contributions: Non-blocking automata processing paradigm enabling parallel symbol processing on GPUs
Prefetching mechanism to increase GPU thread utilization through simultaneous multi-symbol processing
Memoization table approach to eliminate redundant state-symbol computations
Computation privatization strategy to improve data locality and thread-state mapping
primary_theme: GPU-accelerated automata processing through non-blocking parallel execution
